newsitem.title: USA: MGM names Doran president of United Artists unit.
newsitem.headline: MGM names Doran president of United Artists unit.

text.p: Film studio Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Inc said on Wednesday it has picked movie executive Lindsay Doran for the president's position at film product division, United Artist Pictures.

Doran, most recently president of film company Mirage Enterprises, replaces John Calley who resigned from MGM in October to assume the role of president and chief operating officer at Sony Pictures Entertainment.
MGM is jointly owned by investor Kirk Kerkorian's company, Tracinda Corp, and Australian media concern Seven Network Ltd. Sony Pictures is owned by Sony Corp.
At Mirage, which Doran ran with director Sydney Pollack, she produced the recent hit film "Sense and Sensibility" and executive produced movies including "The Firm" and "Sabrina."

"I have known, worked with and respected Lindsay for many years," MGM chairman Frank Mancuso said in a statement. "She combines a love for the art of filmmaking with the creative instincts of an outstanding production executive."
Before her tenure at Mirage, Doran was senior vice president of production at Paramount Pictures.
MGM's other operating divisions include MGM Pictures, MGM Worldwide Television and MGM/UA Distribution Co.
